recent_news.title: Google Signs 617,000 Sq Ft Office Lease at Atrium Place, Gurugram
recent_news.summary: Google leased approximately 617,000 sq ft of premium office space at Atrium Place in one of the largest commercial real estate deals in India in 2025. The deal underscores Atrium Place's position as a top-tier destination for global tech MNCs.

recent_news.title: WeWork India Launches 'WeWork Atrium Place' Co-Working Hub in Gurugram
recent_news.summary: WeWork India launched a 90,000 sq ft co-working center with over 1,200 desks at Atrium Place, Udyog Vihar, leasing space from DLF. This highlights strong flexible workspace demand at the property.

recent_news.title: Daibiru Corporation Invests Rs 10 Billion in Atrium Place
recent_news.summary: Japanese firm Daibiru Corporation (subsidiary of Mitsui O.S.K. Lines) invested Rs 10 billion in Atrium Place, replacing ADIA as an investor via a Hines-facilitated transaction. This signals strong international capital confidence in the project.

flagship_projects.name: Atrium Place
flagship_projects.location: Udyog Vihar Phase V, Sector 19, Gurugram, Haryana, India
key_points: 3.07 million sq ft campus across ~12 acres with 4-5 towers, each 21 floors above ground with 5 basements
Designed by globally renowned Pelli Clarke & Partners; holds LEED Platinum, WELL Platinum, SmartScore Platinum, and WiredScore Platinum pre-certifications
Features a 25-meter-tall climate-controlled central atrium serving as an amenity-rich 'Main Street' with ~100,000 sq ft of retail and F&B
Strategically located off NH-48 with direct connectivity to IGI Airport and Rapid Metro

market_position.positioning_summary: Atrium Place is positioned as India's most premium Grade A+ commercial office development, backed by global real estate giants DLF and Hines and a world-class architect. It targets Fortune 500 and MNC occupiers seeking best-in-class workspace, sustainability credentials, and advanced tech infrastructure in Gurugram's central business district. The project has attracted marquee tenants like Google and WeWork India, firmly establishing it in the ultra-premium segment.
differentiators: Joint venture of DLF (India's largest listed real estate firm) and Hines (global developer with presence in 30+ countries) provides unmatched credibility
Quad-platinum certified (LEED, WELL, SmartScore, WiredScore) — rare in Indian commercial real estate
Designed by Pelli Clarke & Partners, the globally acclaimed architects, adding architectural prestige
25-meter sunlit central atrium with 100,000 sq ft of retail/F&B is a unique lifestyle differentiator for occupants

industry_trends.segment: Grade A+ commercial real estate Gurugram / Delhi-NCR
key_trends: Surging MNC demand: Delhi-NCR recorded 5.1 million sq ft of gross office leasing in Q3 2025, up 56% year-on-year, driven by tech and GCC expansion
ESG and wellness certifications (LEED, WELL, SmartScore) are becoming non-negotiable for global occupiers choosing office space in India
Flexible/co-working space absorption within Grade A buildings is growing, with co-working accounting for 13 million sq ft of Grade A leasing nationally in 2025
Foreign institutional capital (Japanese, Middle Eastern) is actively deploying into Indian commercial real estate, validating premium assets like Atrium Place

comparison_to_competitor.competitor_name: Embassy Manyata Business Park (Embassy Office Parks REIT)
comparison_to_competitor.summary: Embassy Manyata in Bengaluru and Embassy's NCR assets are the closest comparable Grade A+ multi-building campus developments with strong MNC tenant rosters. Embassy REIT benefits from a listed REIT structure providing liquidity and transparency, while Atrium Place is a private JV without public reporting obligations. Atrium Place holds an edge in architectural prestige and newer sustainability certifications, but Embassy REIT's scale (47+ million sq ft portfolio) and brand recall among institutional investors is significantly larger.
notes: Embassy Office Parks REIT has a well-established digital presence and investor relations infrastructure, whereas Atrium Place has minimal standalone online marketing
DLF's own commercial portfolio (Cyber City, DLF Downtown) competes with Atrium Place internally for Gurugram tenants, which could create channel conflict in leasing
